title: First run
summary: Hand the runner to a brain, then pay it for getting closer to the line. Points are all evolution can see.

steps.title: Hand the legs to the brain
steps.body:
The brain named on line 5 is a small neural network. It reads its inputs (eight rays, the way to the finish and the path hint) and answers with two numbers: `brain.move` and `brain.turn`.

Pass them to `act` so the brain moves the runner. Its connections start with random weights, so it moves badly at first. Training is how it gets better.

check.message: Call act with brain.move and brain.turn.

hints: Swap the two zeros for what the brain says.

steps.title: Points for new ground
steps.body:
Training is evolution. Every runner gets a score called fitness, and the brains with the best fitness become the parents of the next generation.

Fitness is the sum of the rewards a runner collects. There are none yet, so every runner scores 0.

`agent.progressGain` is the new ground covered this tick, as a share of the way to the line. Add `reward +10 * agent.progressGain`, so the whole way is worth 10. The test run uses a fixed brain that follows the path hint, and the preview shows it.

check.message: The test run should score more than 5 points.

hints: A reward that pays a little every tick looks like reward +points * amount.
Replace the comment with reward +10 * agent.progressGain.

steps.title: A prize for the line
steps.body:
Getting close is good. Crossing the line is better, and the reward should say so.

`agent.finished` is true on the one tick the runner crosses the line. Add a bonus of 10 points for it. The test runner finishes, so it should now score about 20.

check.message: The test run should score more than 15 points.

hints: A one off reward looks like reward +points when condition.
Replace the comment with reward +10 when agent.finished.
